name: Holmes's Counter-Espionage Service in 1914
description: On the eve of the First World War, Holmes — drawn out of retirement two years earlier by the Foreign Minister and the Premier — completes a long undercover operation against the German agent Von Bork. Posing as the Irish-American spy "Altamont," Holmes has spent two years infiltrating Von Bork's espionage network in England, collecting and corrupting intelligence. He arrests Von Bork on the eve of his planned escape to Germany, hands his apparently sealed dispatches over to British intelligence, and reunites briefly with Watson — who is driving the car. Holmes is then sixty years old. The story is the last canonical chronological appearance of Holmes; the famous "east wind coming, Watson" speech places his career in elegiac context.
